title: Needs, wants, and wishes
description: A simple three-way sort that makes everyday spending decisions much clearer.

body.heading: The three buckets
paragraphs: Needs are things you must have to live, learn, and get around safely. Wants are things that make life nicer but that you could delay or do differently. Wishes are bigger dreams that need time and saving.
Try sorting a week of spending into the three buckets. Most people are surprised by how many small wants quietly add up — not because wants are bad, but because they were invisible.

body.heading: Wants are not the enemy
paragraphs: The point is not to ban wants. Enjoying things is part of life. The point is choosing wants on purpose, within what you can afford, instead of letting every small impulse decide for you.
A good question before buying a want is: will I still be glad about this next week? If the answer is unsure, waiting a day often gives a clearer answer.

body.heading: Wishes need a plan
paragraphs: Wishes — a bike, a trip, a course — become real when they get a name, a rough price, and a small regular saving habit. Even tiny amounts, saved steadily, move a wish closer.

takeaway: Sort spending into needs, wants, and wishes, and choose your wants on purpose.
